content: Analyst derived first-cut sizing (id 1, id 2). Current split: Ibias=30uA, Itail=90uA (mn4=3), I2=120uA (mn5=4). Gain=618 V/V, Noise=16.9mV, PM=69 deg, SR=49 V/us all pass. Only UGBW is binding/violated (79.4 MHz vs 100 MHz target). Next roles should boost gm1 or stage 1 transconductance to reach 100 MHz.

Best id 2 is infeasible only due to ugbw (79.4 MHz vs 100 MHz target, z=-0.115). All other hard constraints pass comfortably (Gain=618, PM=69 deg, SR=49 V/us, Noise=17mV). Chosen lever: boost input pair transconductance gm1 by increasing mn1 multiplicity (from 12 towards 18-20) to lift UGBW above 100 MHz without increasing DC current consumption.

Sizer tested 3 changes on base 2. Id 3 (mn1:18) improved UGBW to 80.95MHz and noise to 13.9mV. Id 4 (cap:0.7pF) further pushed UGBW to 84.79MHz, PM=61.6 deg, SR=56.4V/us, Gain=601.5 (best reward: -0.0597). Id 5 (mn4:4) degraded gain to 54 V/V due to DC operating point shift. Id 4 remains best.

Lesson from id 5: Increasing mn4 tail current without resizing mp1 loads shifts stage 1 output bias, causing mp3 to lose gain (601 -> 54 V/V). To increase gm1 safely, scale mn1 width/multiplicity or scale mp1 alongside mn4.
